newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Britons appeal against drug sentences in Morocco.
newsitem.headline: Britons appeal against drug sentences in Morocco.

text.p: A Briton jailed for five years in Morocco on drug charges had his appeal put off for a week on Wednesday as two British women, one a pregnant teenager, awaited decisions on Thursday over similar terms.
David Richards, 37, from Alnwick, Northumberland, told an appeal court in the northern Moroccan town of Tangier that he knew nothing about 222 kg (489 lbs) of cannabis resin found in his vehicle.
The official news agency MAP said the court announced it would give its decision next Wednesday, October 23.

Richards was arrested with his wife Jill, 40, last August while embarking from Tangier for Spain with their eight-year- old daughter Victoria. He was jailed for five years, fined and his vehicle confiscated.
Jill Richards, who pleaded not guilty, was acquitted.

Meanwhile in the central town of Casablanca, an appeal court on Thursday was due to give its verdict on appeals by hairdresser Sally Louise Griffiths, 18, and barmaid Claire Louise Martin, 28, from Harwich, southeast England.

Arrested on July 30 at Casablanca airport preparing to board a flight to Amsterdam, they were each sentenced last August to five years imprisonment and fined for possessing and trading five kg (11 lbs) of cannabis resin.

The defence, which had sought acquittals at the trial, said on appeal earlier this last week that Griffiths was pregnant, was still an adolescent, had no previous convictions and should benefit from extenuating circumstances.
Police said the two women were promised 1,500 sterling ($2,325) by a British drug dealer in Amsterdam to carry the cannabis from a contact in Fez to the Dutch city.
